title: Simulated crew scenario: 4 fictional crewmembers, MET days 368-412 (seeded, labelled)

source.name: LANDFALL seeded crew scenario, seed 20261114 (ingest/sim_crew.py)
source.license: Apache-2.0 (LANDFALL). Replayed inputs keep their publishers' terms; see their snapshots.
source.citation: LANDFALL simulated crew scenario (seed 20261114), ingest/sim_crew.py, https://github.com/amaroguilherme/landfall. Means calibrated against Barger et al. 2014 (PMID 25127232) and Basner et al. 2011 (PMID 22025811); day-to-day SDs from Flynn-Evans et al. 2016 (PMID 28725719), Quer et al. 2020 (PMID 32023264), Nayan et al. 2012 (PMID 22396364) and Selvin et al. 2007 (PMID 17646610) where published, design choices elsewhere (listed per variable), with context from Knutson et al. 2007 (PMID 17580601), Huang & Redline 2019 (PMID 31167888), Basner et al. 2018 (PMID 29126328), Bellenger et al. 2022 (PMID 36146073), Norsk et al. 2015 (PMID 25774397), Matsui et al. 2012 (PMID 22547439) and Juhanoja et al. 2017 (PMID 28193705); SPE shape from NOAA NCEI GOES-07 EPS (October 1989); Mars-surface baseline from NASA CCMC iSWA MSL RAD; conjunction window modelled from JPL Horizons geometry when present.

caveats: SIMULATED SCENARIO - NOT CREW DATA. Continuous crew vitals are simulated because no public time series of real crew wearable data exists. Every crew value is produced by a seeded generator (seed 20261114; ingest/_sim_model.py) and is identical on every re-run.

Day-to-day noise is realistic, not engineered: every baseline and ordinary day is a plain draw, with nothing trimmed or rejection-sampled. The SDs follow published within-person values where they exist: sleep duration 1.2 h (Flynn-Evans et al. 2016: ISS actigraphy, all crewmembers pooled, so an upper-side value), resting heart rate 3.0 bpm (Quer et al. 2020), 24-h urine output 342 mL (derived from Nayan et al. 2012) and fasting glucose 5.7% (Selvin et al. 2007). The midpoint, PVT-B, HRV, skin temperature, light, fluid and blood-pressure SDs are design choices, each listed with its context in data.variables[*].calibration. Mean sleep is calibrated against Barger et al. 2014 and the PVT-B lapse definition against Basner et al. 2011; episode values are ours.

More day-to-day noise lowers Tier B's sensitivity: the smallest one-day change a personal band can flag is critical x SD x sqrt(1 + 1/n), 4.37 baseline SDs on a 14-day baseline, printed per crewmember and indicator in data.self_check.tier_b.per_crew (mdc). The chance false-alarm rate does not grow with the noise: it is alpha = 0.001 per indicator-day (alpha/2 for a caution) only if day-to-day noise were normal and independent. Skewed data break that, so PVT-B lapse counts are tested on the Anscombe scale and the sleep midpoint as a signed shift in both directions; the measured rate of every indicator under this noise model is in data.self_check.chance_rates, and engine/rules/personal.json declares it where it is not within 0.5-2 times the printed one (rci.caveat, chance_rate).

What Tier B finds in this data (data.self_check, recomputed on every build): renal_hydration (CM-3, case renal_stone): urine_volume_24h: Tier B flags no scripted day (detection probability per scripted day under this noise model 0.49-0.63); Tier A target_urine_output_24h is outside on day(s) 398-401; fluid_intake_24h: Tier B flags no scripted day (detection probability per scripted day under this noise model 0.32-0.52). sleep_shift (CM-1, case sleep_circadian): sleep_duration: Tier B flags no scripted day (detection probability per scripted day under this noise model 0.00-0.00); sleep_midpoint_shift: Tier B flags MET day(s) 404-412 (detection probability per scripted day under this noise model 0.39-0.58); pvt_lapses: Tier B flags no scripted day (detection probability per scripted day under this noise model 0.00-0.10); pvt_median_rt: Tier B flags no scripted day (detection probability per scripted day under this noise model 0.00-0.01). Unscripted reliable changes (chance, from realistic day-to-day noise): CM-1 skin_temp day 385 (t = 4.792, critical 4.221, increase, nominal); CM-3 sleep_midpoint_shift day 407 (t = 4.305, critical 4.221, increase, caution). Case openings caused by chance flags alone (the app opens a case at a trigger's caution and labels a single-indicator, single-day Tier B opening 'Possibly chance'): CM-3 sleep_circadian on MET day 407 (sleep_midpoint_shift, t = 4.305; no scripted episode). Chance rates with no real change (data.self_check.chance_rates, seeded Monte Carlo with this noise model, every indicator): all within 0.5-2.0 times the printed rate except pvt_lapses (caution 0.45x, flag 0.24x), mood (caution 0.99x, flag 0.495x), whose measured multipliers engine/rules/personal.json declares (chance_rate).
CM-1..CM-4 are fictional: no names, no real PII. Mood is simulated for everyone, private by default and never alerts.

Daily values are stamped when their measurement window closes, so 'now' (MET 412/14:20:00) has no 24-h urine, fluid or daytime-light value for day 412 yet: that day is incomplete. Cuff blood pressure and fingerstick glucose are manual readings from the vehicle medical kit, daily on the 14 baseline days (MET 368-381), then twice a week (MET days 382, 385, 389, 392, 396, 399, 403, 406, 410), 30 min after wake, seated, before breakfast.

Blood pressure and glucose: NASA-STD-3001 publishes no numeric in-flight alert thresholds for crew health; its alert requirements leave the number to the program. LANDFALL compares this reading only with the crewmember's own baseline (Tier B, caution at most), never with a population cut-off. The glucose calibration lists the Inspiration4 lab reference range as context only, never as an alert limit.
career_effective_dose is a design-choice prior (mSv), not a calculation. The SPE day's absorbed dose rate (µGy/day) is never converted to effective dose: LANDFALL makes no personal dose projection.

SPE day: the event TIME PROFILE is REAL (NOAA NCEI GOES-7 >10 MeV proton flux, October 1989, read from swpc_spe_replay) and only time-shifted, so its first S3-level sample lands at MET 412/14:15:00. vehicle.series.proton_flux_10mev carries that replayed flux unchanged as the reading of an EXTERNAL space-weather monitor above the Martian atmosphere (in Mars orbit, relayed to the habitat locally, no Earth link needed; an external monitor of the kind [V2 6165] describes, reporting one ≥10 MeV channel). Scenario assumption: NO radial-distance and NO atmospheric correction is applied; GOES measured in Earth orbit, and a real event at Mars would give a different flux. A monitor on the surface would read far less, because the atmosphere absorbs most lower-energy protons. Every replayed sample, before and after 'now', carries provenance 'replay'.

vehicle.series.onboard_dose_rate is a SIMULATED habitat dose rate that confirms the external reading inside the habitat: the same flux profile under an assumed 10x scaling (design choice), not a radiation-transport calculation and not a measurement. LANDFALL is not the radiation alarm: the vehicle radiation monitoring system alerts the crew ([V2 6164]); LANDFALL opens the health case that follows and guides the crew.

SPE day: the quiet-time baseline is REAL: the median MSL RAD 'dose_e_total' dose rate, 184.73 µGy/day, read from hapi_msl_rad_dose. The flux-to-dose scaling (S3 flux = 10x baseline) is an ASSUMPTION, not a radiation-transport calculation.

Calendar: MET day 412 is mapped into a Mars solar-conjunction window MODELLED from JPL Horizons geometry (horizons_mars_comms: 2028-03-12T12:00:00Z to 2028-03-29T23:00:00Z; window edges fitted to NASA's published command moratoria, RMS 0.79 d); the mission, its launch date (MET epoch) and the pairing with the 1989 event are fictional.

generator.rng: random.Random(f'{seed}:{stream}') per crewmember x variable; random() and gauss() only
generator.seed_policy: the project seed, fixed before this noise model was written; it was not re-drawn to improve detections or to remove chance flags

met.format: MET strings are ddd/hh:mm:ss with no leading zeros in the day field (NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 F.6.1 f)
met.convention: MET = integer seconds since MET epoch; day = floor(MET / 86400), so MET day 412 starts at 35,596,800 s

record.min_elongation_basis: smallest of the daily 00:00 UTC samples (not a refined minimum)
record.basis: derived: Sun-Earth-Mars elongation below the calibrated threshold (edges linearly interpolated between daily samples, rounded to the hour)

calendar.selection: first modelled window starting on/after 2026-11-14 that is >= 10 d 06 h long (else the latest long-enough one, else the longest); now = window stop - 11 d 06 h (window long enough)
calendar.window_basis: modelled from JPL Horizons geometry (Sun-Earth-Mars elongation below a threshold whose edges are fitted to NASA's published command moratoria); not an operational window

source.arithmetic: linear interpolation between the daily 00:00 UTC rows around now_utc

input.title: Earth-Mars light time and solar conjunction windows, 2026-2029 (JPL Horizons)
input.publisher: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Solar System Dynamics Group

observation_format.expand: for each series: observation = {crew_id, variable, value: v[i], unit, t: t[i] (or start_t + i*step_s), source, provenance: the series' own 'provenance' when it has one (vehicle proton_flux_10mev: 'replay', before and after 'now'), else 'simulated'}; vehicle series have crew_id null
observation_format.t_meaning: MET seconds when the value became available (end of its measurement window)
observation_format.missing: null = no sample (a gap to show as stale/missing per [V2 10020]); never zero

sleep_duration.label: Sleep duration (actigraphy)
sleep_duration.cadence: daily (main sleep episode, stamped at wake)
sleep_duration.definition: Total sleep time of the main sleep episode ending on that MET day, from band actigraphy.

source.citation: Barger LK, Flynn-Evans EE, Kubey A, Walsh L, Ronda JM, Wang W, Wright KP Jr, Czeisler CA. Prevalence of sleep deficiency and use of hypnotic drugs in astronauts before, during, and after spaceflight: an observational study. Lancet Neurol 2014;13(9):904-912. doi:10.1016/S1474-4422(14)70122-X. PMID 25127232
source.note: ISS crew obtained 6.09 h (SD 0.67) of actigraphic sleep per night in flight.

source.citation: Flynn-Evans EE, Barger LK, Kubey AA, Sullivan JP, Czeisler CA. Circadian misalignment affects sleep and medication use before and during spaceflight. NPJ Microgravity 2016;2:15019. doi:10.1038/npjmgrav.2015.19. PMID 28725719
source.note: Table 3: in-flight ISS actigraphic sleep 6.4 h (s.d. 1.2) on circadian-aligned and 5.4 h (s.d. 1.4) on misaligned sleep episodes (21 astronauts, 3,248 in-flight days). Those episodes come from all crewmembers together, so the SD also holds differences between crewmembers: an upper-side estimate of one person's night-to-night SD.

source.citation: Knutson KL, Rathouz PJ, Yan LL, Liu K, Lauderdale DS. Intra-individual daily and yearly variability in actigraphically recorded sleep measures: the CARDIA study. Sleep 2007;30(6):793-796. doi:10.1093/sleep/30.6.793. PMID 17580601
source.note: Within-subject daily SD of actigraphic sleep duration, 669 adults aged 38-50 (CARDIA).

source.rationale: Keeps rare tail draws physically plausible for a fixed sleep period.

calibration.item: CM-1 after the day-403 schedule shift

source.rationale: Scripted short sleep opportunity (about 5 h in bed); same order as the 4-h time-in-bed partial sleep deprivation protocol used to validate the PVT-B (Basner 2011). Not tuned for Tier B.

sleep_midpoint_shift.label: Sleep midpoint shift (signed)
sleep_midpoint_shift.definition: Signed difference, in hours, between the night's sleep midpoint and the median midpoint of the crewmember's baseline nights (MET days 368-381), with clock arithmetic across midnight, wrapped to [-12, 12) h: positive is later, negative is earlier. Tier B tests it in both directions (engine/rules/personal.json: worse = either).

source.rationale: No published within-crewmember value was found. Free-living older adults averaged a 58-min weekday sleep-onset SD in MESA (next entry); a fixed mission sleep period should be more regular. At the MESA value Tier B would rarely flag CM-1's shift (data.self_check, tier_b_detection_probability_at_alt_sd).

calibration.value: 58 min weekday sleep-onset SD (64 min over 7 days)

source.citation: Huang T, Redline S. Cross-sectional and prospective associations of actigraphy-assessed sleep regularity with metabolic abnormalities: the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis. Diabetes Care 2019;42(8):1422-1429. doi:10.2337/dc19-0596. PMID 31167888
source.note: Mean 7-day SD in 2,003 MESA participants; the paper reports that sleep-onset and sleep-midpoint SDs correlate at r = 0.97.

source.rationale: Places the sleep episodes (data.crew[*].sleep_episodes) on the MET clock; the emitted shift is measured from the baseline median, not from 02:00. Subtracting that one median moves every value by the same amount, so the shift keeps the midpoint's own day-to-day noise.
Partial adaptation to a 3-h later schedule. Not tuned for Tier B.

pvt_lapses.label: PVT-B lapses
pvt_lapses.definition: Number of responses with reaction time >= 355 ms on the 3-min PVT-B (a count).

source.citation: Basner M, Mollicone D, Dinges DF. Validity and sensitivity of a brief psychomotor vigilance test (PVT-B) to total and partial sleep deprivation. Acta Astronaut 2011;69(11-12):949-959. doi:10.1016/j.actaastro.2011.07.015. PMID 22025811
source.note: The paper lowers the PVT-B lapse threshold from 500 ms to 355 ms. No NASA standard adopts 355 ms; it is attributed to the paper only.

calibration.value: Poisson counts, mean 0.9-1.2 lapses per test

source.rationale: A count, not a normal variable: one Poisson draw per test. Tier B tests it on the Anscombe scale, 2 sqrt(x + 3/8) (engine/rules/personal.json transform), and its measured chance rate under this model is in data.self_check.chance_rates. No published rested PVT-B lapse rate at 355 ms was used.

A moderate rise, in line with the medium effect size Basner et al. 2011 report for 5 nights of 4 h in bed (0.76 for PVT-B lapses at the 355-ms threshold); the exact values are ours. Not tuned for Tier B.

pvt_median_rt.label: PVT-B median reaction time
pvt_median_rt.definition: Median reaction time of the 3-min PVT-B, in ms.

source.rationale: Plausible values; not fitted.
No published within-person day-to-day SD of the 3-min PVT-B median was found; 14 ms is ours.

source.citation: Basner M, Hermosillo E, Nasrini J, McGuire S, Saxena S, Moore TM, Gur RC, Dinges DF. Repeated administration effects on psychomotor vigilance test performance. Sleep 2018;41(1):zsx187. doi:10.1093/sleep/zsx187. PMID 29126328
source.note: Mean and median RT, response speed and lapses did not change systematically over 16 PVT-B administrations, so no learning trend is added.

source.rationale: Moderate slowing that accompanies the lapse rise. Not tuned for Tier B.

light_exposure_daytime.label: Daytime light exposure
light_exposure_daytime.cadence: daily (wake period, stamped at the next sleep onset)
light_exposure_daytime.definition: Mean photopic illuminance over the wake period, from the band light sensor.

calibration.value: 229-251 lux, day-to-day SD 20% of the mean

source.rationale: No verified habitat illuminance value was used; unchanged through the episodes. A non-alerting context indicator.

resting_hr.label: Resting heart rate
resting_hr.cadence: daily (main sleep episode, stamped at wake)
resting_hr.definition: Lowest stable 5-min heart rate during the main sleep episode, from band PPG inter-beat intervals (engine/rules/personal.json).

source.rationale: Plausible values; not fitted.

source.citation: Quer G, Gouda P, Galarnyk M, Topol EJ, Steinhubl SR. Inter- and intraindividual variability in daily resting heart rate and its associations with age, sex, sleep, BMI, and time of year: retrospective, longitudinal cohort study of 92,457 adults. PLoS One 2020;15(2):e0227709. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0227709. PMID 32023264
source.note: Average within-individual SD of daily resting HR over time: 3.03 bpm (3.10 women, 2.90 men), wrist-worn trackers, median 320 days per person. It spans seasons, so a 2-week SD may be slightly smaller.

hrv_sdnn.label: HRV (SDNN)
hrv_sdnn.cadence: daily (main sleep episode, stamped at wake)
hrv_sdnn.definition: Pulse-rate variability: the SD of the band's PPG (optical pulse) inter-beat intervals in 5-min (300-s) windows during the main sleep episode, averaged. It stands in for heart rate variability; it is not computed from ECG normal-to-normal intervals.

source.rationale: Short windows in sleep keep recording conditions comparable from night to night.
Plausible values; not fitted.

No published night-to-night SD of sleep SDNN was found. For context, Bellenger et al. 2022 report a mean 7-day CV of 5.4% for overnight ln RMSSD (a log-scale index) and 7.6% for overnight HR in elite athletes (next entry).

source.citation: Bellenger CR, Miller D, Halson SL, Roach GD, Maclennan M, Sargent C. Evaluating the typical day-to-day variability of WHOOP-derived heart rate variability in Olympic water polo athletes. Sensors (Basel) 2022;22(18):6723. doi:10.3390/s22186723. PMID 36146073
source.note: WHOOP-derived overnight values, 11 elite water polo players, 16 weeks.

skin_temp.label: Skin temperature
skin_temp.cadence: daily (main sleep episode, stamped at wake)
skin_temp.definition: Median skin temperature during the main sleep episode, from the band.

source.rationale: Plausible values; not fitted. Skin temperature follows cabin temperature and clothing, so it is a non-alerting context indicator.

urine_volume_24h.label: 24-h urine output
urine_volume_24h.cadence: daily (MET-midnight to MET-midnight collection, stamped at its end)
urine_volume_24h.definition: Volume of the 24-h urine collection for that MET day, entered manually.

calibration.value: outside below 1,500 mL/day; approaching below 2,500 mL/day

source.rationale: The levels are owned and sourced by rule target_urine_output_24h in engine/rules/thresholds.json (NASA HRP Evidence Report, Risk of Renal Stone Formation); the generator never tunes values to them, except that it refuses to ship an unscripted day below 1,500 mL, which would open a case nobody scripted.
A crew following the hydration countermeasure, whose target is 2.5-3 L/day of urine (quoted by rule target_urine_output_24h).

source.citation: Norsk P, Asmar A, Damgaard M, Christensen NJ. Fluid shifts, vasodilatation and ambulatory blood pressure reduction during long duration spaceflight. J Physiol 2015;593(3):573-584. doi:10.1113/jphysiol.2014.284869. PMID 25774397
source.note: Table 1: 24-h urine volume of eight ISS astronauts in flight (1,978 mL preflight).

source.arithmetic: sd = mean |difference| x sqrt(pi) / 2 = 385.4 x 0.8862 = 341.6 mL (two independent normal days: E|X1 - X2| = 2 sd / sqrt(pi))

inputs.citation: Nayan M, Elkoushy MA, Andonian S. Variations between two 24-hour urine collections in patients presenting to a tertiary stone clinic. Can Urol Assoc J 2012;6(1):30-33. doi:10.5489/cuaj.11131. PMID 22396364
inputs.note: Table 1: mean absolute difference between two consecutive-day 24-h urine volumes, 385.4 mL (95% CI 334.3-436.5), 188 stone-clinic patients.

source.rationale: Below the 1,500 mL/day level on every episode day (the scripted Tier A crossing). Not tuned for Tier B: whether it is also a reliable change against CM-3's own noisy baseline is tested in data.self_check.

fluid_intake_24h.label: 24-h fluid intake
fluid_intake_24h.cadence: daily (same window as the urine collection)
fluid_intake_24h.definition: Logged fluid intake for that MET day.

source.rationale: Intake exceeds output by food water, sweat and insensible losses; plausible, not fitted.

source.arithmetic: the day's urine noise (341.6 mL, shared: drinking drives output) plus an independent 150-mL spread of intake minus output: sqrt(341.6^2 + 150^2) = 373 mL

inputs.citation: Nayan M, Elkoushy MA, Andonian S. Variations between two 24-hour urine collections in patients presenting to a tertiary stone clinic. Can Urol Assoc J 2012;6(1):30-33. doi:10.5489/cuaj.11131. PMID 22396364

source.rationale: Intake falls with output, as SPEC section 7 describes.

mood.label: Mood (self-report)
mood.cadence: daily at the 12:00 MET check-in (Noon Sight)
mood.definition: Self-rated mood, integer 1-5. PRIVATE by default and NON-ALERTING (SPEC 3.3, 7).

calibration.value: mostly 3-4; CM-1 dips to 2-3 during the sleep episode

source.rationale: Never alerts; excluded from the ground packet unless the crewmember consents.

bp_systolic.label: Blood pressure, systolic (cuff)
bp_systolic.cadence: daily on the 14 baseline days (MET 368-381), then twice a week (MET days 382, 385, 389, 392, 396, 399, 403, 406, 410), 30 min after wake, seated, before breakfast
bp_systolic.definition: Systolic pressure of a seated cuff reading from the vehicle medical kit, taken by the crewmember and entered manually.
bp_systolic.nasa_limit: NASA-STD-3001 publishes no numeric in-flight alert thresholds for crew health; its alert requirements leave the number to the program. LANDFALL compares this reading only with the crewmember's own baseline (Tier B, caution at most), never with a population cut-off.

source.rationale: Healthy-adult values; not fitted.

calibration.value: 24-h systolic 8 ± 2 mmHg below preflight on ISS

source.citation: Norsk P, Asmar A, Damgaard M, Christensen NJ. Fluid shifts, vasodilatation and ambulatory blood pressure reduction during long duration spaceflight. J Physiol 2015;593(3):573-584. doi:10.1113/jphysiol.2014.284869. PMID 25774397
source.note: Ambulatory 24-h averages of eight ISS astronauts (mean ± SE); systolic 8 ± 2, diastolic 9 ± 2 mmHg lower in space.

source.rationale: No day-to-day home-BP SD of healthy crew-age adults was found to use directly. Context: the within-individual SD of 5-day home systolic BP was 6.3-7.1 mmHg in treated hypertensive patients (Matsui et al. 2012), and a day-to-day CV above 11.0% systolic / 12.8% diastolic marks the top decile of 6,238 adults (Juhanoja et al. 2017).

source.citation: Matsui Y, O'Rourke MF, Hoshide S, Ishikawa J, Shimada K, Kario K. Combined effect of angiotensin II receptor blocker and either a calcium channel blocker or diuretic on day-by-day variability of home blood pressure: the Japan Combined Treatment With Olmesartan and a Calcium-Channel Blocker Versus Olmesartan and Diuretics Randomized Efficacy Study. Hypertension 2012;59(6):1132-1138. doi:10.1161/HYPERTENSIONAHA.111.189217. PMID 22547439

calibration.value: top decile: day-to-day CV > 11.0% systolic, > 12.8% diastolic

source.citation: Juhanoja EP, Niiranen TJ, Johansson JK, Puukka PJ, Thijs L, Asayama K, Langén VL, Hozawa A, Aparicio LS, Ohkubo T, Tsuji I, Imai Y, Stergiou GS, Jula AM, Staessen JA; IDHOCO Investigators. Outcome-driven thresholds for increased home blood pressure variability. Hypertension 2017;69(4):599-607. doi:10.1161/HYPERTENSIONAHA.116.08603. PMID 28193705

calibration.value: daily for the 14 baseline days, then twice a week

source.rationale: A 14-value baseline gives this indicator the same single-case test as the daily ones (n = 14, df 13); twice a week afterwards keeps the measurement burden low.

bp_diastolic.label: Blood pressure, diastolic (cuff)
bp_diastolic.cadence: daily on the 14 baseline days (MET 368-381), then twice a week (MET days 382, 385, 389, 392, 396, 399, 403, 406, 410), 30 min after wake, seated, before breakfast
bp_diastolic.definition: Diastolic pressure of the same seated cuff reading, entered manually.
bp_diastolic.nasa_limit: NASA-STD-3001 publishes no numeric in-flight alert thresholds for crew health; its alert requirements leave the number to the program. LANDFALL compares this reading only with the crewmember's own baseline (Tier B, caution at most), never with a population cut-off.

source.rationale: Healthy-adult values; not fitted.
See bp_systolic; the correlation keeps the two pressures of one reading moving together.

source.citation: Juhanoja EP, Niiranen TJ, Johansson JK, Puukka PJ, Thijs L, Asayama K, Langén VL, Hozawa A, Aparicio LS, Ohkubo T, Tsuji I, Imai Y, Stergiou GS, Jula AM, Staessen JA; IDHOCO Investigators. Outcome-driven thresholds for increased home blood pressure variability. Hypertension 2017;69(4):599-607. doi:10.1161/HYPERTENSIONAHA.116.08603. PMID 28193705

glucose.label: Fasting glucose (fingerstick)
glucose.cadence: daily on the 14 baseline days (MET 368-381), then twice a week (MET days 382, 385, 389, 392, 396, 399, 403, 406, 410), 30 min after wake, seated, before breakfast
glucose.definition: Capillary glucose from a fingerstick glucometer, fasting, taken by the crewmember and entered manually.
glucose.nasa_limit: NASA-STD-3001 publishes no numeric in-flight alert thresholds for crew health; its alert requirements leave the number to the program. LANDFALL compares this reading only with the crewmember's own baseline (Tier B, caution at most), never with a population cut-off.

source.rationale: Healthy fasting values; not fitted.

source.citation: Selvin E, Crainiceanu CM, Brancati FL, Coresh J. Short-term variability in measures of glycemia and implications for the classification of diabetes. Arch Intern Med 2007;167(14):1545-1551. doi:10.1001/archinte.167.14.1545. PMID 17646610
source.note: Within-person CV 5.7% (95% CI 5.3-6.1) for repeat fasting tests about 2 weeks apart, 685 adults without diagnosed diabetes (NHANES III).

source.rationale: Fingerstick meters add their own error; 3% is ours.

inputs.citation: Selvin E, Crainiceanu CM, Brancati FL, Coresh J. Short-term variability in measures of glycemia and implications for the classification of diabetes. Arch Intern Med 2007;167(14):1545-1551. doi:10.1001/archinte.167.14.1545. PMID 17646610

source.arithmetic: glucose reference range printed with every Inspiration4 comprehensive metabolic panel sample (OSD-575); the same on every sample. Context only, not an alert limit.

vo2max.label: VO2max (periodic fitness test)
vo2max.definition: Aerobic capacity from the periodic in-flight fitness test.

source.rationale: Set by SPEC section 7 for the FFD demo: within the [V1 4001] microgravity-EVA floor (32.9) and outside the [V1 4002] surface-EVA floor (36.5). The floors themselves live in thresholds.json.
Comfortably above both floors so only CM-2 flips with the environment selector.

career_effective_dose.label: Career effective dose to date (prior)
career_effective_dose.cadence: one value per crewmember, at MET 412/00:00
career_effective_dose.definition: Career effective dose to date before the SPE day, as it would come from the dosimetry record.

source.rationale: Not computed from any transport model. Chosen below 480 mSv (80% of the [V1 4030] 600 mSv limit) so the SPE case is driven by the event, not by the career limit. The SPE day's absorbed dose is NOT added: LANDFALL does not convert µGy to mSv.

heart_rate.label: Heart rate (1-min)
heart_rate.cadence: PT1M, MET day 412 only, 00:00 to now
heart_rate.definition: 1-min mean heart rate from band PPG inter-beat intervals.

source.rationale: Plausible values; the sleep segment sits just above that night's resting_hr (the lowest stable 5-min rate).

cabin_ppco2.label: Cabin ppCO2 (1-h mean)
cabin_ppco2.definition: 1-hour mean cabin CO2 partial pressure; value k covers [start + k h, start + (k+1) h).

source.rationale: Kept below the 2.4 mmHg approach level of rule pel_cabin_ppco2_1h in engine/rules/thresholds.json (and the [V2 6004] 1-h mean limit of 3 mmHg) so it never competes with the scripted cases.

onboard_dose_rate.label: Habitat dose rate (simulated confirmation)

source.rationale: A monitor on the surface would not read this flux: the Martian atmosphere absorbs most lower-energy protons, so the ≥10 MeV flux at the surface follows only the high-energy tail. The scenario therefore takes the S3 reading from an external monitor above the atmosphere, an external monitor of the kind [V2 6165] describes (one ≥10 MeV channel, not the full spectra), relayed to the habitat without an Earth link. The habitat dose rate is a separate simulated confirmation.

source.rationale: Scenario assumption: Mars is farther from the Sun than Earth and no heliocentric-distance scaling is applied; no atmospheric transport is applied either (the reading is above the atmosphere). A real event at Mars would give a different flux.

noise_model.note: Day-to-day noise is a plain draw from the noise model on every baseline and ordinary day; nothing is trimmed or rejection-sampled. More noise lowers Tier B's sensitivity (its smallest flaggable change, critical x SD x sqrt(1 + 1/n), grows with the SD); it does not raise the chance false-alarm rate, which stays at alpha under normal, independent noise. The realized chance rate of every indicator under this model is measured in data.self_check.chance_rates.

episodes.summary: 24-h urine output falls below 1,500 mL/day (the outside level of rule target_urine_output_24h in engine/rules/thresholds.json) on MET days 398-401 while fluid intake falls as well; both recover from day 402. The Tier A target crossing is scripted; whether Tier B also flags the drop is tested, not assumed (data.self_check).

On MET day 403 CM-1's work schedule shifts 3 h later and the sleep opportunity is shortened to about 5 h (vehicle-operations support). From the night ending on day 404 sleep is about 4.3-4.6 h, its midpoint sits about 2.3-2.6 h later than the baseline nights, and PVT-B lapses and median reaction time rise moderately. The episode is still running at 'now' (no countermeasure is applied in the data, so the case can be acted on in the demo). There is no Tier A rule for any of these indicators: if Tier B does not flag them, nothing does (data.self_check).

ffd_demo.expect: within the microgravity-EVA floor (32.9, [V1 4001]); outside the surface-EVA floor (36.5, [V1 4002])

self_check.method: SPEC section 5 single-case t (Crawford & Howell 1998): t = (x - mean) / (sd * sqrt(1 + 1/n)), sd = sample SD (n-1), df = n - 1, on the indicator's declared test scale (PVT-B lapses: the Anscombe transform 2 sqrt(x + 3/8)); reliable when |t| > the two-tailed critical value at alpha 0.001. Baseline = the crewmember's observations whose measurement day, floor((t - 1) / 86400), is in MET days 368-381; every later observation is tested against it, as the engine and app do.
self_check.mdc_formula: smallest one-day change a band can flag = critical x SD x sqrt(1 + 1/n) (= 4.37 baseline SDs at n = 14, on the test scale)
self_check.detection_probability_method: seeded Monte Carlo, 2000 fresh 14-day baselines from the generator's own noise model per scripted day; share in which Tier B flags the scripted value in the worse direction
summary: renal_hydration (CM-3, case renal_stone): urine_volume_24h: Tier B flags no scripted day (detection probability per scripted day under this noise model 0.49-0.63); Tier A target_urine_output_24h is outside on day(s) 398-401; fluid_intake_24h: Tier B flags no scripted day (detection probability per scripted day under this noise model 0.32-0.52).

sleep_shift (CM-1, case sleep_circadian): sleep_duration: Tier B flags no scripted day (detection probability per scripted day under this noise model 0.00-0.00); sleep_midpoint_shift: Tier B flags MET day(s) 404-412 (detection probability per scripted day under this noise model 0.39-0.58); pvt_lapses: Tier B flags no scripted day (detection probability per scripted day under this noise model 0.00-0.10); pvt_median_rt: Tier B flags no scripted day (detection probability per scripted day under this noise model 0.00-0.01).

Unscripted reliable changes (chance, from realistic day-to-day noise): CM-1 skin_temp day 385 (t = 4.792, critical 4.221, increase, nominal); CM-3 sleep_midpoint_shift day 407 (t = 4.305, critical 4.221, increase, caution).

Case openings caused by chance flags alone (the app opens a case at a trigger's caution and labels a single-indicator, single-day Tier B opening 'Possibly chance'): CM-3 sleep_circadian on MET day 407 (sleep_midpoint_shift, t = 4.305; no scripted episode).

Chance rates with no real change (data.self_check.chance_rates, seeded Monte Carlo with this noise model, every indicator): all within 0.5-2.0 times the printed rate except pvt_lapses (caution 0.45x, flag 0.24x), mood (caution 0.99x, flag 0.495x), whose measured multipliers engine/rules/personal.json declares (chance_rate).

tier_b_detection_probability_at_alt_sd.basis: MESA weekday sleep-onset SD, 58 min (Huang & Redline 2019); onset and midpoint SDs correlate at r = 0.97

chance_rates.method: for every Tier B indicator, the share of tests with no real change that flag: a worse-direction reliable change (a caution on an alerting indicator; both directions for worse = either) and a reliable change in either direction, each divided by its nominal rate (alpha/2, or alpha for either; alpha). Laid out like the scenario (fixed 14-day baseline, then 31 days each tested against it), on the indicator's declared test scale, with this generator's own noise model: 5,000 seeded 45-day records per crewmember and indicator. engine/tests/test_chance_rates.py replays the same records through the engine and requires the same counts.
